paper.title: SQLBarber: A System Leveraging Large Language Models to Generate Customized and Realistic SQL Workloads
paper.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data

summary.text: SQLBarber generates customised, realistic SQL workloads with large language models. The motivation is that real queries are hard to obtain for privacy reasons and existing generators offer little customisation or ability to meet realistic constraints. SQLBarber provides a declarative interface, removes the need to write SQL templates by hand while accepting natural-language constraints on them, and adds a self-correction pipeline that profiles, refines and prunes templates by query cost. The authors open-source ten benchmarks built from Snowflake and Amazon Redshift statistics.
summary.relationship_to_sqlancer: Workload generation for benchmarking rather than correctness oracles; SQLancer is cited among SQL generation work.
supporting_excerpts: However, acquiring real-world SQL queries is challenging due to privacy concerns, and existing generation methods offer limited options for customization and for satisfying realistic constraints.
To address this issue, we present SQLBarber, a system based on Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate customized and realistic SQL workloads.
It reduces query generation time by one to two orders of magnitude and significantly improves alignment with the target cost distribution, compared with existing methods.

sources.note: Semantic Scholar records this paper as citing the publication that introduced Query Plan Guidance (QPG).
